newsitem.title: USA: Golf-Daly, Love shoot 66s to lead PGA, Allenby clo.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Daly, Love shoot 66s to lead PGA, Allenby clo.

text.p: se
By Walter Bagley

John Daly, who quit in the middle of the last major championship he played, shot a record-tying four-under-par 66 on Thursday to lead the PGA Championship -- only to watch Davis Love catch him at the end of the day.

Daly, a recovering alcoholic who walked off the course after 27 holes in the U.S. Open in June because he had the shakes due to drinking, took advantage of perfect early playing conditions to match the Winged Foot Golf Club course record that his friend Fuzzy Zoeller set in winning the 1984 U.S. Open.

The rejuvenated Daly then waited the rest of the day while most of the 150 professionals in the field failed to overtake him -- until early evening, when Love birdied the last two holes to also shoot 66 in fading light.
Their record performances outshone the "dream threesome" of the day -- Tiger Woods, Ernie Els and Justin Leonard, the young winners of the year's first three majors, who all remained in the hunt.
Robert Allenby of Australia also made a late-day bid to overtake Daly but he bogeyed Winged Foot's difficult 18th to card the day's only 67.
Love said he was delighted to be able to tame Winged Foot late in the day when playing conditions are usually most difficult, especially the spike-marked greens.
"I think that's the hardest time to do it," Love said of playing well late. "But I knew if John could get it done there was the possibilty of a low score for me."
Still, the big story was Daly, who began his mercurial career with a stunning victory in the 1991 PGA Championship.
"I hit a lot of fairways and made some putts," Daly said modestly after posting an impressive seven birdies on Winged Foot's vaunted West Course against three bogeys.
The 31-year-old Daly, who won the 1995 British Open in a playoff for his second major title, said Wednesday's sporadic rains had softened the greens and made them more receptive to approach shots.

"The greens were perfect this morning," said the newly slimmed-down Daly, who did not have a birdie putt longer than 15 feet. "They were softer than yesterday, which made it easier to throw the ball right at the flag."
Daly saved the best for last as he closed with three consecutive birdies -- with putts of five feet, four feet and one foot, after hitting two 156-yard nine irons and a 137-yard pitching wedge.
"That just made my day," Daly said. "It's just a wonderful feeling to birdie all three of those holes." All three measure 448 yards or longer.

Love, one of the best players yet to win a major, burst into contention on the front nine when he went five under par in four holes starting at the second. He punctuated the spree with an eagle at the 515-yard fifth, where he drained a 20-foot putt from off the fringe.

Veteran Tom Kite, the 47-year-old U.S. Ryder Cup captain, and two former PGA Championship winners, Paul Azinger and Bob Tway -- along with British Open champion Leonard -- all shot 68s on a warm, sunny day.

They were later joined by Greg Norman, Chris Perry, Paul Stankowski and Shigeki Maruyama of Japan in staying close to Daly, who was a complete unknown six years ago when he won the PGA at Crooked Stick Golf Club in Indiana -- after being the ninth alternate.
Another 11 players were tied at 69, including former U.S. Open champions Lee Janzen and Steve Jones, Phil Mickelson and Costantino Rocca of Italy, who lost to Daly in the 1995 British Open playoff.

Leonard, 25, won the day's unofficial match among the winners of the year's first three majors when his 69 outscored Masters champion Woods and U.S. Open winner Els. They are all in the same threesome for the first two rounds.

Woods, 21, and South African Els, 27, both matched par 70 after adventurous rounds in which each made a double bogey, Els at the 442-yard eighth and Woods at the 540-yard 12th. They were in a big group at level-par 70.

After getting off to a fast start with three consecutive birdies on the front nine, Woods, playing in his first PGA Championship, gave those strokes back in two holes coming home -- the double at 12 and a bogey at 14.

Els, who won his second U.S. Open at Congressional Country Club, also struggled after a good start. He was three under after seven holes but then went five over in the next seven before he righted himself with birdies at 16 and 18.
But the day belonged to Daly, who underwent his second bout of alcohol rehabilitation this spring.
"I'm always scared what's going to happen next, so I don't want to get too excited," he said. "It's basically one day at a time and one shot at a time."
